newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs seen facing profit-taking, mood upbeat.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs seen facing profit-taking, mood upbeat.

text.p: Expectations that the economy will recover are likely to keep Seoul stocks bullish on Thursday but profit-taking will increase, brokers said.
On Wednesday, the composite index rose 2.54 percent, or 19.26 points, to 777.29 on the optimism sparked by the release of June trade balance figures this week.

"The overall sentiment will remain strong as investors believe the market has room to rise further," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities. "But we see a strong profit-taking selling once the index tops the 780 level."

Korea Electric Power and selective construction firms are expected to attract buying interest after the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation and North Korea signed technical and policy agreements overnight, brokers said.

Under the ageements, preparatory work will begin within weeks in North Korea for the construction of two light-water nuclear reactors. South Korean officials have said local companies are expected to lead the work.
